BRIEF NOTE ON LIVE STORAGE STATUS OF 166 RESERVOIRS IN THE COUNTRY (WITH REFERENCE TO
RESERVOIR STORAGE BULLETIN OF 02.04.2026)
1. ALL INDIA STATUS
Central Water Commission is monitoring live storage status of 166 reservoirs of the country and is issuing
weekly bulletin on every Thursday. Out of these reservoirs, 20 reservoirs are of hydro-electric projects
having total live storage capacity of 35.299 BCM. The total live storage capacity of 166 reservoirs is
183.565 BCM which is about 71.20% of the live storage capacity of 257.812 BCM which is estimated to
have been created in the country. As per reservoir storage bulletin dated 02.04.2026, live storage
available in these reservoirs is 85.698 BCM, which is 46.69% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. However, last year the live storage available in these reservoirs for the corresponding period
was 73.597 BCM and Normal* storage was 67.656 BCM. Thus, the live storage available in 166
reservoirs as per 02.04.2026 Bulletin is 116.44% of the live storage of corresponding period of last year
and 126.67% of Normal storage.
As per Table-01, the overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the
country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.
2. REGION WISE STORAGE STATUS
a) NORTHERN REGION
The northern region includes States of Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Rajasthan. There are 11 reservoirs
under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 19.836 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage
Bulletin dated 02.04.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 8.750 BCM which is
44.11% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last
year was 22.59% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 31.61% of live storage capacity
of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is better than the corresponding period of last year
and is also better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
b) EASTERN REGION
The Eastern region includes States of Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Odisha,
Tripura and West Bengal . There are 27 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage
capacity of 21.759 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 02.04.2026, the total live storage
available in these reservoirs is 9.752 BCM which is 44.82% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was 38.10% and Normal storage during
corresponding period was 45.36% of live storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during
current year is better than the corresponding period of last year but is less than Normal storage during
the corresponding period
c) WESTERN REGION
The Western region includes States of Goa, Gujarat and Maharashtra. There are 53 reservoirs under CWC
monitoring having total live storage capacity of 38.094 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated
02.04.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 21.308 BCM which is 55.94 % of total
live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was
48.48% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 41.09% of live storage capacity of these
1

reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is better than the storage of last year and is also better
than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
d) CENTRAL REGION
The Central region includes States of Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
There are 28 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 48.588 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 02.04.2026, the total live storage available in these eservoirs is 25.943
BCM which is 53.39% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 45.32% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 40.50% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus,storage during current year is better than the storage of last
year and is also better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
e) SOUTHERN REGION
The Southern region includes States of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.
There are 47 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 55.288 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 02.04.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 19.945
BCM which is 36.07% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 36.78% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 29.27% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is less than the storage of last
year but is better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
The region wise and reservoir wise details are given in the following pages of the Bulletin.

Based on the data available for 166 reservoirs as per Reservoir Storage bulletin dated 02.04.2026, the
total live storage of the country has been estimated to be 120.360 BCM against 257.812 BCM which is
estimated to have been created in the country.

d) CENTRAL REGION
The Central region includes States of Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
There are 28 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 48.588 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 02.07.2026, the total live storage available in these eservoirs is 15.654
BCM which is 32.22% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 32.56% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 27.31% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus,storage during current year is less than the storage of last year
but is better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
e) SOUTHERN REGION
The Southern region includes States of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.
There are 47 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 55.288 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 02.07.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 11.233
BCM which is 20.32% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 53.92% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 26.16% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is less than the storage of last
year and is also less than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
The region wise and reservoir wise details are given in the following pages of the Bulletin.

BRIEF NOTE ON LIVE STORAGE STATUS OF 166 RESERVOIRS IN THE COUNTRY (WITH REFERENCE TO
RESERVOIR STORAGE BULLETIN OF 04.06.2026)
1. ALL INDIA STATUS
Central Water Commission is monitoring live storage status of 166 reservoirs of the country and is issuing
weekly bulletin on every Thursday. Out of these reservoirs, 20 reservoirs are of hydro-electric projects
having total live storage capacity of 35.299 BCM. The total live storage capacity of 166 reservoirs is
183.565 BCM which is about 71.20% of the live storage capacity of 257.812 BCM which is estimated to
have been created in the country. As per reservoir storage bulletin dated 04.06.2026, live storage
available in these reservoirs is 54.726 BCM, which is 29.81% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. However, last year the live storage available in these reservoirs for the corresponding period
was 58.303 BCM and Normal* storage was 46.152 BCM. Thus, the live storage available in 166
reservoirs as per 04.06.2026 Bulletin is 93.86% of the live storage of corresponding period of last year
and 118.58% of Normal storage.
As per Table-01, the overall storage position is less than the corresponding period of last year in the
country as a whole but is better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.
2. REGION WISE STORAGE STATUS
a) NORTHERN REGION
The northern region includes States of Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Rajasthan. There are 11 reservoirs
under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 19.836 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage
Bulletin dated 04.06.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 7.524 BCM which is
37.93% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last
year was 29.76% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 28.91% of live storage capacity
of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is better than the corresponding period of last year
and is also better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
b) EASTERN REGION
The Eastern region includes States of Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Odisha,
Tripura and West Bengal . There are 27 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage
capacity of 21.759 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 04.06.2026, the total live storage
available in these reservoirs is 5.050 BCM which is 23.21% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was 25.66% and Normal storage during
corresponding period was 26.04% of live storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during
current year is less than the corresponding period of last year and is also less than Normal storage
during the corresponding period
c) WESTERN REGION
The Western region includes States of Goa, Gujarat and Maharashtra. There are 53 reservoirs under CWC
monitoring having total live storage capacity of 38.094 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated
04.06.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 12.700 BCM which is 33.34 % of total
live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was
33.20% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 24.04% of live storage capacity of these
1

reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is better than the storage of last year and is also better
than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
d) CENTRAL REGION
The Central region includes States of Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
There are 28 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 48.588 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 04.06.2026, the total live storage available in these eservoirs is 17.473
BCM which is 35.96% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 30.98% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 28.60% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus,storage during current year is better than the storage of last
year and is also better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
e) SOUTHERN REGION
The Southern region includes States of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.
There are 47 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 55.288 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 04.06.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 11.979
BCM which is 21.67% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 34.58% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 21.16% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is less than the storage of last
year but is better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
The region wise and reservoir wise details are given in the following pages of the Bulletin.

BRIEF NOTE ON LIVE STORAGE STATUS OF 166 RESERVOIRS IN THE COUNTRY (WITH REFERENCE TO
RESERVOIR STORAGE BULLETIN OF 06.08.2026)
1. ALL INDIA STATUS
Central Water Commission is monitoring live storage status of 166 reservoirs of the country and is issuing
weekly bulletin on every Thursday. Out of these reservoirs, 20 reservoirs are of hydro-electric projects
having total live storage capacity of 35.299 BCM. The total live storage capacity of 166 reservoirs is
183.565 BCM which is about 71.20% of the live storage capacity of 257.812 BCM which is estimated to
have been created in the country. As per reservoir storage bulletin dated 06.08.2026, live storage
available in these reservoirs is 96.966 BCM, which is 52.82% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. However, last year the live storage available in these reservoirs for the corresponding period
was 132.368 BCM and Normal* storage was 99.831 BCM. Thus, the live storage available in 166
reservoirs as per 06.08.2026 Bulletin is 73.25% of the live storage of corresponding period of last year
and 97.13% of Normal storage.
As per Table-01, the overall storage position is less than the corresponding period of last year in the
country as a whole and is also less than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.
2. REGION WISE STORAGE STATUS
a) NORTHERN REGION
The northern region includes States of Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Rajasthan. There are 11 reservoirs
under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 19.836 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage
Bulletin dated 06.08.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 9.084 BCM which is
45.80% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last
year was 70.43% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 53.47% of live storage capacity
of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is less than the corresponding period of last year
and is also less than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
b) EASTERN REGION
The Eastern region includes States of Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Odisha,
Tripura and West Bengal . There are 27 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage
capacity of 21.759 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 06.08.2026, the total live storage
available in these reservoirs is 10.268 BCM which is 47.19% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was 54.97% and Normal storage during
corresponding period was 42.76% of live storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during
current year is less than the corresponding period of last year but is better than Normal storage during
the corresponding period
c) WESTERN REGION
The Western region includes States of Goa, Gujarat and Maharashtra. There are 53 reservoirs under CWC
monitoring having total live storage capacity of 38.094 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated
06.08.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 28.899 BCM which is 75.86 % of total
live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was
73.76% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 56.64% of live storage capacity of these
1

reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is better than the storage of last year and is also better
than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
d) CENTRAL REGION
The Central region includes States of Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
There are 28 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 48.588 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 06.08.2026, the total live storage available in these eservoirs is 23.022
BCM which is 47.38% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 72.53% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 54.98% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus,storage during current year is less than the storage of last year
and is also less than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
e) SOUTHERN REGION
The Southern region includes States of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.
There are 47 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 55.288 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 06.08.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 25.693
BCM which is 46.47% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 77.96% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 57.21% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is less than the storage of last
year and is also less than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
The region wise and reservoir wise details are given in the following pages of the Bulletin.

BRIEF NOTE ON LIVE STORAGE STATUS OF 166 RESERVOIRS IN THE COUNTRY (WITH REFERENCE TO
RESERVOIR STORAGE BULLETIN OF 09.07.2026)
1. ALL INDIA STATUS
Central Water Commission is monitoring live storage status of 166 reservoirs of the country and is issuing
weekly bulletin on every Thursday. Out of these reservoirs, 20 reservoirs are of hydro-electric projects
having total live storage capacity of 35.299 BCM. The total live storage capacity of 166 reservoirs is
183.565 BCM which is about 71.20% of the live storage capacity of 257.812 BCM which is estimated to
have been created in the country. As per reservoir storage bulletin dated 09.07.2026, live storage
available in these reservoirs is 59.443 BCM, which is 32.38% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. However, last year the live storage available in these reservoirs for the corresponding period
was 93.587 BCM and Normal* storage was 55.232 BCM. Thus, the live storage available in 166
reservoirs as per 09.07.2026 Bulletin is 63.52% of the live storage of corresponding period of last year
and 107.62% of Normal storage.
As per Table-01, the overall storage position is less than the corresponding period of last year in the
country as a whole but is better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.
2. REGION WISE STORAGE STATUS
a) NORTHERN REGION
The northern region includes States of Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Rajasthan. There are 11 reservoirs
under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 19.836 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage
Bulletin dated 09.07.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 6.195 BCM which is
31.23% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last
year was 42.31% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 32.71% of live storage capacity
of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is less than the corresponding period of last year
and is also less than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
b) EASTERN REGION
The Eastern region includes States of Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Odisha,
Tripura and West Bengal . There are 27 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage
capacity of 21.759 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 09.07.2026, the total live storage
available in these reservoirs is 5.972 BCM which is 27.45% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was 44.38% and Normal storage during
corresponding period was 27.22% of live storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during
current year is less than the corresponding period of last year but is better than Normal storage during
the corresponding period
c) WESTERN REGION
The Western region includes States of Goa, Gujarat and Maharashtra. There are 53 reservoirs under CWC
monitoring having total live storage capacity of 38.094 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated
09.07.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 16.182 BCM which is 42.48 % of total
live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was
52.92% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 28.74% of live storage capacity of these
1

reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is less than the storage of last year but is better than the
normal storage during the corresponding period.
d) CENTRAL REGION
The Central region includes States of Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
There are 28 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 48.588 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 09.07.2026, the total live storage available in these eservoirs is 17.480
BCM which is 35.98% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 45.29% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 31.25% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus,storage during current year is less than the storage of last year
but is better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
e) SOUTHERN REGION
The Southern region includes States of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.
There are 47 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 55.288 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 09.07.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 13.614
BCM which is 24.62% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 60.36% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 30.18% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is less than the storage of last
year and is also less than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
The region wise and reservoir wise details are given in the following pages of the Bulletin.

BRIEF NOTE ON LIVE STORAGE STATUS OF 166 RESERVOIRS IN THE COUNTRY (WITH REFERENCE TO
RESERVOIR STORAGE BULLETIN OF 11.06.2026)
1. ALL INDIA STATUS
Central Water Commission is monitoring live storage status of 166 reservoirs of the country and is issuing
weekly bulletin on every Thursday. Out of these reservoirs, 20 reservoirs are of hydro-electric projects
having total live storage capacity of 35.299 BCM. The total live storage capacity of 166 reservoirs is
183.565 BCM which is about 71.20% of the live storage capacity of 257.812 BCM which is estimated to
have been created in the country. As per reservoir storage bulletin dated 11.06.2026, live storage
available in these reservoirs is 51.917 BCM, which is 28.28% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. However, last year the live storage available in these reservoirs for the corresponding period
was 56.533 BCM and Normal* storage was 44.834 BCM. Thus, the live storage available in 166
reservoirs as per 11.06.2026 Bulletin is 91.83% of the live storage of corresponding period of last year
and 115.80% of Normal storage.
As per Table-01, the overall storage position is less than the corresponding period of last year in the
country as a whole but is better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.
2. REGION WISE STORAGE STATUS
a) NORTHERN REGION
The northern region includes States of Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Rajasthan. There are 11 reservoirs
under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 19.836 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage
Bulletin dated 11.06.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 6.672 BCM which is
33.64% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last
year was 28.67% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 28.79% of live storage capacity
of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is better than the corresponding period of last year
and is also better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
b) EASTERN REGION
The Eastern region includes States of Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Odisha,
Tripura and West Bengal . There are 27 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage
capacity of 21.759 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 11.06.2026, the total live storage
available in these reservoirs is 4.736 BCM which is 21.77% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was 24.57% and Normal storage during
corresponding period was 24.22% of live storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during
current year is less than the corresponding period of last year and is also less than Normal storage
during the corresponding period
c) WESTERN REGION
The Western region includes States of Goa, Gujarat and Maharashtra. There are 53 reservoirs under CWC
monitoring having total live storage capacity of 38.094 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated
11.06.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 11.858 BCM which is 31.13 % of total
live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was
30.07% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 22.80% of live storage capacity of these
1

reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is better than the storage of last year and is also better
than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
d) CENTRAL REGION
The Central region includes States of Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
There are 28 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 48.588 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 11.06.2026, the total live storage available in these eservoirs is 17.049
BCM which is 35.09% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 30.33% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 27.62% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus,storage during current year is better than the storage of last
year and is also better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
e) SOUTHERN REGION
The Southern region includes States of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.
There are 47 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 55.288 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 11.06.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 11.602
BCM which is 20.98% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 34.93% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 21.24% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is less than the storage of last
year and is also less than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
The region wise and reservoir wise details are given in the following pages of the Bulletin.

BRIEF NOTE ON LIVE STORAGE STATUS OF 166 RESERVOIRS IN THE COUNTRY (WITH REFERENCE TO
RESERVOIR STORAGE BULLETIN OF 14.05.2026)
1. ALL INDIA STATUS
Central Water Commission is monitoring live storage status of 166 reservoirs of the country and is issuing
weekly bulletin on every Thursday. Out of these reservoirs, 20 reservoirs are of hydro-electric projects
having total live storage capacity of 35.299 BCM. The total live storage capacity of 166 reservoirs is
183.565 BCM which is about 71.20% of the live storage capacity of 257.812 BCM which is estimated to
have been created in the country. As per reservoir storage bulletin dated 14.05.2026, live storage
available in these reservoirs is 63.232 BCM, which is 34.45% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. However, last year the live storage available in these reservoirs for the corresponding period
was 56.002 BCM and Normal* storage was 51.052 BCM. Thus, the live storage available in 166
reservoirs as per 14.05.2026 Bulletin is 112.91% of the live storage of corresponding period of last year
and 123.86% of Normal storage.
As per Table-01, the overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the
country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.
2. REGION WISE STORAGE STATUS
a) NORTHERN REGION
The northern region includes States of Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Rajasthan. There are 11 reservoirs
under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 19.836 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage
Bulletin dated 14.05.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 8.206 BCM which is
41.37% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last
year was 28.14% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 30.01% of live storage capacity
of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is better than the corresponding period of last year
and is also better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
b) EASTERN REGION
The Eastern region includes States of Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Odisha,
Tripura and West Bengal . There are 27 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage
capacity of 21.759 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 14.05.2026, the total live storage
available in these reservoirs is 6.567 BCM which is 30.18% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was 26.40% and Normal storage during
corresponding period was 31.36% of live storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during
current year is better than the corresponding period of last year but is less than Normal storage during
the corresponding period
c) WESTERN REGION
The Western region includes States of Goa, Gujarat and Maharashtra. There are 53 reservoirs under CWC
monitoring having total live storage capacity of 38.094 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated
14.05.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 15.336 BCM which is 40.26 % of total
live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was
33.22% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 27.95% of live storage capacity of these
1

reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is better than the storage of last year and is also better
than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
d) CENTRAL REGION
The Central region includes States of Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
There are 28 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 48.588 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 14.05.2026, the total live storage available in these eservoirs is 19.072
BCM which is 39.25% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 34.45% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 32.15% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus,storage during current year is better than the storage of last
year and is also better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
e) SOUTHERN REGION
The Southern region includes States of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.
There are 47 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 55.288 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 14.05.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 14.051
BCM which is 25.41% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 27.65% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 21.72% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is less than the storage of last
year but is better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
The region wise and reservoir wise details are given in the following pages of the Bulletin.

estimated to have been created in the country.

BRIEF NOTE ON LIVE STORAGE STATUS OF 166 RESERVOIRS IN THE COUNTRY (WITH REFERENCE TO
RESERVOIR STORAGE BULLETIN OF 18.06.2026)
1. ALL INDIA STATUS
Central Water Commission is monitoring live storage status of 166 reservoirs of the country and is issuing
weekly bulletin on every Thursday. Out of these reservoirs, 20 reservoirs are of hydro-electric projects
having total live storage capacity of 35.299 BCM. The total live storage capacity of 166 reservoirs is
183.565 BCM which is about 71.20% of the live storage capacity of 257.812 BCM which is estimated to
have been created in the country. As per reservoir storage bulletin dated 18.06.2026, live storage
available in these reservoirs is 50.457 BCM, which is 27.49% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. However, last year the live storage available in these reservoirs for the corresponding period
was 58.249 BCM and Normal* storage was 44.646 BCM. Thus, the live storage available in 166
reservoirs as per 18.06.2026 Bulletin is 86.62% of the live storage of corresponding period of last year
and 113.02% of Normal storage.
As per Table-01, the overall storage position is less than the corresponding period of last year in the
country as a whole but is better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.
2. REGION WISE STORAGE STATUS
a) NORTHERN REGION
The northern region includes States of Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Rajasthan. There are 11 reservoirs
under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 19.836 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage
Bulletin dated 18.06.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 6.579 BCM which is
33.17% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last
year was 29.21% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 28.54% of live storage capacity
of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is better than the corresponding period of last year
and is also better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
b) EASTERN REGION
The Eastern region includes States of Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Odisha,
Tripura and West Bengal . There are 27 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage
capacity of 21.759 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 18.06.2026, the total live storage
available in these reservoirs is 4.545 BCM which is 20.89% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was 23.50% and Normal storage during
corresponding period was 23.59% of live storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during

BRIEF NOTE ON LIVE STORAGE STATUS OF 166 RESERVOIRS IN THE COUNTRY (WITH REFERENCE TO
RESERVOIR STORAGE BULLETIN OF 21.05.2026)
1. ALL INDIA STATUS
Central Water Commission is monitoring live storage status of 166 reservoirs of the country and is issuing
weekly bulletin on every Thursday. Out of these reservoirs, 20 reservoirs are of hydro-electric projects
having total live storage capacity of 35.299 BCM. The total live storage capacity of 166 reservoirs is
183.565 BCM which is about 71.20% of the live storage capacity of 257.812 BCM which is estimated to
have been created in the country. As per reservoir storage bulletin dated 21.05.2026, live storage
available in these reservoirs is 60.830 BCM, which is 33.14% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. However, last year the live storage available in these reservoirs for the corresponding period
was 54.337 BCM and Normal* storage was 48.901 BCM. Thus, the live storage available in 166

BRIEF NOTE ON LIVE STORAGE STATUS OF 166 RESERVOIRS IN THE COUNTRY (WITH REFERENCE TO
RESERVOIR STORAGE BULLETIN OF 23.07.2026)
1. ALL INDIA STATUS
Central Water Commission is monitoring live storage status of 166 reservoirs of the country and is issuing
weekly bulletin on every Thursday. Out of these reservoirs, 20 reservoirs are of hydro-electric projects
having total live storage capacity of 35.299 BCM. The total live storage capacity of 166 reservoirs is
183.565 BCM which is about 71.20% of the live storage capacity of 257.812 BCM which is estimated to
have been created in the country. As per reservoir storage bulletin dated 23.07.2026, live storage
available in these reservoirs is 70.432 BCM, which is 38.37% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. However, last year the live storage available in these reservoirs for the corresponding period
was 110.519 BCM and Normal* storage was 75.661 BCM. Thus, the live storage available in 166
reservoirs as per 23.07.2026 Bulletin is 63.73% of the live storage of corresponding period of last year
and 93.09% of Normal storage.
As per Table-01, the overall storage position is less than the corresponding period of last year in the
country as a whole and is also less than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.
2. REGION WISE STORAGE STATUS
a) NORTHERN REGION
The northern region includes States of Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Rajasthan. There are 11 reservoirs
under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 19.836 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage
Bulletin dated 23.07.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 7.057 BCM which is
35.58% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last
year was 50.18% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 41.04% of live storage capacity
of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is less than the corresponding period of last year
and is also less than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
b) EASTERN REGION
The Eastern region includes States of Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Odisha,
Tripura and West Bengal . There are 27 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage
capacity of 21.759 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 23.07.2026, the total live storage
available in these reservoirs is 8.246 BCM which is 37.90% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was 47.72% and Normal storage during
corresponding period was 33.26% of live storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during
current year is less than the corresponding period of last year but is better than Normal storage during
the corresponding period
c) WESTERN REGION
The Western region includes States of Goa, Gujarat and Maharashtra. There are 53 reservoirs under CWC
monitoring having total live storage capacity of 38.094 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated
23.07.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 19.398 BCM which is 50.92 % of total
live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was
61.48% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 42.05% of live storage capacity of these
1

reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is less than the storage of last year but is better than the
normal storage during the corresponding period.
d) CENTRAL REGION
The Central region includes States of Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
There are 28 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 48.588 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 23.07.2026, the total live storage available in these eservoirs is 19.002
BCM which is 39.11% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 58.40% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 40.82% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus,storage during current year is less than the storage of last year
and is also less than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
e) SOUTHERN REGION
The Southern region includes States of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.
There are 47 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 55.288 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 23.07.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 16.729
BCM which is 30.26% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 69.43% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 44.18% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is less than the storage of last
year and is also less than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
The region wise and reservoir wise details are given in the following pages of the Bulletin.

BRIEF NOTE ON LIVE STORAGE STATUS OF 166 RESERVOIRS IN THE COUNTRY (WITH REFERENCE TO
RESERVOIR STORAGE BULLETIN OF 25.06.2026)
1. ALL INDIA STATUS
Central Water Commission is monitoring live storage status of 166 reservoirs of the country and is issuing
weekly bulletin on every Thursday. Out of these reservoirs, 20 reservoirs are of hydro-electric projects
having total live storage capacity of 35.299 BCM. The total live storage capacity of 166 reservoirs is
183.565 BCM which is about 71.20% of the live storage capacity of 257.812 BCM which is estimated to
have been created in the country. As per reservoir storage bulletin dated 25.06.2026, live storage
available in these reservoirs is 48.405 BCM, which is 26.37% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. However, last year the live storage available in these reservoirs for the corresponding period
was 66.114 BCM and Normal* storage was 45.808 BCM. Thus, the live storage available in 166
reservoirs as per 25.06.2026 Bulletin is 73.21% of the live storage of corresponding period of last year
and 105.67% of Normal storage.
As per Table-01, the overall storage position is less than the corresponding period of last year in the
country as a whole but is better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.
2. REGION WISE STORAGE STATUS
a) NORTHERN REGION
The northern region includes States of Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Rajasthan. There are 11 reservoirs
under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 19.836 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage
Bulletin dated 25.06.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 6.066 BCM which is
30.58% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last
year was 31.89% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 28.25% of live storage capacity
of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is less than the corresponding period of last year
but is better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
b) EASTERN REGION
The Eastern region includes States of Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Odisha,
Tripura and West Bengal . There are 27 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage
capacity of 21.759 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 25.06.2026, the total live storage
available in these reservoirs is 4.334 BCM which is 19.92% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was 29.89% and Normal storage during
corresponding period was 24.87% of live storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during
current year is less than the corresponding period of last year and is also less than Normal storage
during the corresponding period
c) WESTERN REGION
The Western region includes States of Goa, Gujarat and Maharashtra. There are 53 reservoirs under CWC
monitoring having total live storage capacity of 38.094 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated
25.06.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 10.862 BCM which is 28.51 % of total
live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was
37.69% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 22.36% of live storage capacity of these
1

reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is less than the storage of last year but is better than the
normal storage during the corresponding period.
d) CENTRAL REGION
The Central region includes States of Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
There are 28 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 48.588 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 25.06.2026, the total live storage available in these eservoirs is 15.667
BCM which is 32.24% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 29.29% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 26.46% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus,storage during current year is better than the storage of last
year and is also better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
e) SOUTHERN REGION
The Southern region includes States of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.
There are 47 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 55.288 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 25.06.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 11.476
BCM which is 20.76% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 44.67% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 24.27% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is less than the storage of last
year and is also less than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
The region wise and reservoir wise details are given in the following pages of the Bulletin.

BRIEF NOTE ON LIVE STORAGE STATUS OF 166 RESERVOIRS IN THE COUNTRY (WITH REFERENCE TO
RESERVOIR STORAGE BULLETIN OF 27.03.2026)
1. ALL INDIA STATUS
Central Water Commission is monitoring live storage status of 166 reservoirs of the country and is issuing
weekly bulletin on every Thursday. Out of these reservoirs, 20 reservoirs are of hydro-electric projects
having total live storage capacity of 35.299 BCM. The total live storage capacity of 166 reservoirs is
183.565 BCM which is about 71.20% of the live storage capacity of 257.812 BCM which is estimated to
have been created in the country. As per reservoir storage bulletin dated 27.03.2026, live storage
available in these reservoirs is 85.432 BCM, which is 46.54% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. However, last year the live storage available in these reservoirs for the corresponding period
was 77.314 BCM and Normal* storage was 70.587 BCM. Thus, the live storage available in 166
reservoirs as per 27.03.2026 Bulletin is 110.50% of the live storage of corresponding period of last year
and 121.03% of Normal storage.
As per Table-01, the overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the
country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.
2. REGION WISE STORAGE STATUS
a) NORTHERN REGION
The northern region includes States of Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Rajasthan. There are 11 reservoirs
under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 19.836 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage
Bulletin dated 27.03.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 8.845 BCM which is
44.59% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last
year was 23.86% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 32.12% of live storage capacity
of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is better than the corresponding period of last year
and is also better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
b) EASTERN REGION
The Eastern region includes States of Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Odisha,
Tripura and West Bengal . There are 27 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage
capacity of 21.759 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 27.03.2026, the total live storage
available in these reservoirs is 10.349 BCM which is 47.56% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was 40.11% and Normal storage during
corresponding period was 47.19% of live storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during
current year is better than the corresponding period of last year and is also better than Normal storage
during the corresponding period
c) WESTERN REGION
The Western region includes States of Goa, Gujarat and Maharashtra. There are 53 reservoirs under CWC
monitoring having total live storage capacity of 38.094 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated
27.03.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 22.863 BCM which is 60.02 % of total
live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was
51.40% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 43.22% of live storage capacity of these
1

reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is better than the storage of last year and is also better
than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
d) CENTRAL REGION
The Central region includes States of Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
There are 28 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 48.588 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 27.03.2026, the total live storage available in these eservoirs is 22.256
BCM which is 45.81% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 46.83% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 41.71% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus,storage during current year is less than the storage of last year
but is better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
e) SOUTHERN REGION
The Southern region includes States of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.
There are 47 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 55.288 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 27.03.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 21.119
BCM which is 38.20% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 38.92% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 31.14% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is less than the storage of last
year but is better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
The region wise and reservoir wise details are given in the following pages of the Bulletin.
3. BROAD ANALYSIS OF OTHER TABLES IN THE BULLETIN
Normal storage means average storage of last ten years, Close to normal storage means where shortfall is
upto 20% of normal, deficient storage is where shortfall is more than 20% of the normal and upto 60% of
the normal, highly deficient means where shortfall is more than 60% of normal.
In the table on page 10, better than normal storage is available in Ganga, Indus, Mahi, Tapi, Krishna,

Subarnarekha. Close to Normal in Narmada, Brahmani & baitarni. Deficient in Barak & other and Highly

BRIEF NOTE ON LIVE STORAGE STATUS OF 166 RESERVOIRS IN THE COUNTRY (WITH REFERENCE TO
RESERVOIR STORAGE BULLETIN OF 29.05.2026)
1. ALL INDIA STATUS
Central Water Commission is monitoring live storage status of 166 reservoirs of the country and is issuing
weekly bulletin on every Thursday. Out of these reservoirs, 20 reservoirs are of hydro-electric projects
having total live storage capacity of 35.299 BCM. The total live storage capacity of 166 reservoirs is
183.565 BCM which is about 71.20% of the live storage capacity of 257.812 BCM which is estimated to
have been created in the country. As per reservoir storage bulletin dated 29.05.2026, live storage
available in these reservoirs is 56.300 BCM, which is 30.67% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. However, last year the live storage available in these reservoirs for the corresponding period
was 55.892 BCM and Normal* storage was 47.269 BCM. Thus, the live storage available in 166
reservoirs as per 29.05.2026 Bulletin is 100.73% of the live storage of corresponding period of last year
and 119.11% of Normal storage.
As per Table-01, the overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the
country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.
2. REGION WISE STORAGE STATUS
a) NORTHERN REGION
The northern region includes States of Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Rajasthan. There are 11 reservoirs
under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 19.836 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage
Bulletin dated 29.05.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 7.694 BCM which is
38.79% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last
year was 29.18% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 29.01% of live storage capacity
of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is better than the corresponding period of last year
and is also better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
b) EASTERN REGION
The Eastern region includes States of Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Odisha,
Tripura and West Bengal . There are 27 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage
capacity of 21.759 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 29.05.2026, the total live storage
available in these reservoirs is 5.323 BCM which is 24.46% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was 24.67% and Normal storage during
corresponding period was 27.37% of live storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during
current year is less than the corresponding period of last year and is also less than Normal storage
during the corresponding period
c) WESTERN REGION

monitoring having total live storage capacity of 38.094 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated
29.05.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 13.625 BCM which is 35.77 % of total
live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was
31.63% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 24.86% of live storage capacity of these

BRIEF NOTE ON LIVE STORAGE STATUS OF 166 RESERVOIRS IN THE COUNTRY (WITH REFERENCE TO
RESERVOIR STORAGE BULLETIN OF 30.04.2026)
1. ALL INDIA STATUS
Central Water Commission is monitoring live storage status of 166 reservoirs of the country and is issuing
weekly bulletin on every Thursday. Out of these reservoirs, 20 reservoirs are of hydro-electric projects
having total live storage capacity of 35.299 BCM. The total live storage capacity of 166 reservoirs is
183.565 BCM which is about 71.20% of the live storage capacity of 257.812 BCM which is estimated to
have been created in the country. As per reservoir storage bulletin dated 30.04.2026, live storage
available in these reservoirs is 71.082 BCM, which is 38.72% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. However, last year the live storage available in these reservoirs for the corresponding period
was 62.296 BCM and Normal* storage was 56.176 BCM. Thus, the live storage available in 166
reservoirs as per 30.04.2026 Bulletin is 114.10% of the live storage of corresponding period of last year
and 126.53% of Normal storage.
As per Table-01, the overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the
country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.
2. REGION WISE STORAGE STATUS
a) NORTHERN REGION
The northern region includes States of Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Rajasthan. There are 11 reservoirs
under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 19.836 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage
Bulletin dated 30.04.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 8.593 BCM which is
43.32% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last
year was 23.44% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 31.05% of live storage capacity
of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is better than the corresponding period of last year
and is also better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
b) EASTERN REGION
The Eastern region includes States of Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Odisha,
Tripura and West Bengal . There are 27 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage
capacity of 21.759 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 30.04.2026, the total live storage
available in these reservoirs is 7.481 BCM which is 34.38% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was 29.29% and Normal storage during
corresponding period was 35.43% of live storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during
current year is better than the corresponding period of last year but is less than Normal storage during
the corresponding period
c) WESTERN REGION
The Western region includes States of Goa, Gujarat and Maharashtra. There are 53 reservoirs under CWC
monitoring having total live storage capacity of 38.094 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated
30.04.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 17.187 BCM which is 45.12 % of total
live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was
37.54% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 31.97% of live storage capacity of these
1

reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is better than the storage of last year and is also better
than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
d) CENTRAL REGION
The Central region includes States of Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
There are 28 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 48.588 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 30.04.2026, the total live storage available in these eservoirs is 22.241
BCM which is 45.77% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 41.42% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 35.34% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus,storage during current year is better than the storage of last
year and is also better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
e) SOUTHERN REGION
The Southern region includes States of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.
There are 47 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 55.288 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 30.04.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 15.580
BCM which is 28.18% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 30.47% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 23.44% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is less than the storage of last
year but is better than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
The region wise and reservoir wise details are given in the following pages of the Bulletin.

BRIEF NOTE ON LIVE STORAGE STATUS OF 166 RESERVOIRS IN THE COUNTRY (WITH REFERENCE TO
RESERVOIR STORAGE BULLETIN OF 30.07.2026)
1. ALL INDIA STATUS
Central Water Commission is monitoring live storage status of 166 reservoirs of the country and is issuing
weekly bulletin on every Thursday. Out of these reservoirs, 20 reservoirs are of hydro-electric projects
having total live storage capacity of 35.299 BCM. The total live storage capacity of 166 reservoirs is
183.565 BCM which is about 71.20% of the live storage capacity of 257.812 BCM which is estimated to
have been created in the country. As per reservoir storage bulletin dated 30.07.2026, live storage
available in these reservoirs is 81.479 BCM, which is 44.39% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. However, last year the live storage available in these reservoirs for the corresponding period
was 124.634 BCM and Normal* storage was 87.624 BCM. Thus, the live storage available in 166
reservoirs as per 30.07.2026 Bulletin is 65.37% of the live storage of corresponding period of last year
and 92.99% of Normal storage.
As per Table-01, the overall storage position is less than the corresponding period of last year in the
country as a whole and is also less than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.
2. REGION WISE STORAGE STATUS
a) NORTHERN REGION
The northern region includes States of Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Rajasthan. There are 11 reservoirs
under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 19.836 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage
Bulletin dated 30.07.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 8.139 BCM which is
41.03% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last
year was 58.79% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 46.51% of live storage capacity
of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is less than the corresponding period of last year
and is also less than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
b) EASTERN REGION
The Eastern region includes States of Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Odisha,
Tripura and West Bengal . There are 27 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage
capacity of 21.759 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 30.07.2026, the total live storage
available in these reservoirs is 9.924 BCM which is 45.61% of total live storage capacity of these
reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was 51.22% and Normal storage during
corresponding period was 37.10% of live storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during
current year is less than the corresponding period of last year but is better than Normal storage during
the corresponding period
c) WESTERN REGION
The Western region includes States of Goa, Gujarat and Maharashtra. There are 53 reservoirs under CWC
monitoring having total live storage capacity of 38.094 BCM. As per Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated
30.07.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 23.668 BCM which is 62.13 % of total
live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding period of last year was
71.14% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 49.40% of live storage capacity of these

reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is less than the storage of last year but is better than the
normal storage during the corresponding period.
d) CENTRAL REGION
The Central region includes States of Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
There are 28 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 48.588 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 30.07.2026, the total live storage available in these eservoirs is 21.100
BCM which is 43.43% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 68.05% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 46.89% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus,storage during current year is less than the storage of last year
and is also less than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
e) SOUTHERN REGION
The Southern region includes States of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.
There are 47 reservoirs under CWC monitoring having total live storage capacity of 55.288 BCM. As per
Reservoir Storage Bulletin dated 30.07.2026, the total live storage available in these reservoirs is 18.648
BCM which is 33.73% of total live storage capacity of these reservoirs. The storage during corresponding
period of last year was 75.36% and Normal storage during corresponding period was 51.96% of live
storage capacity of these reservoirs. Thus, storage during current year is less than the storage of last
year and is also less than the normal storage during the corresponding period.
